Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: one transparent sprite frame for a 2D pixel-art RPG enemy
Input images: Image 1 is the approved Ruins String Puppet identity anchor and is authoritative for character design, proportions, materials and palette. Image 2 is the approved active slap pose and is a secondary same-character action reference. Keep the same puppet from both images.
Character identity: one slender marionette made from aged dark walnut wood, narrow carved mask-like head with dark eye slits, compact jointed torso, asymmetrical articulated limbs, one distinctly long forward/right arm ending in a broad wooden palm, shorter rear/left arm, a few snapped oxidized-copper strings hanging from back and shoulders, restrained moss-olive flecks, charcoal joints and muted warm highlights.
Style: crisp 2D pixel-art game sprite with clean dark outlines, sharp edges, readable chunky pixel clusters and a limited muted palette matching the references; no painterly haze and no 3D rendering.
Composition: exactly one complete full-body side-view puppet, facing right with face toward the right, centered on a square canvas at the same character scale as Image 1; keep the whole head, every limb, feet, palm and snapped strings inside frame with generous transparent padding; no cropping.
Background and effects: genuine transparent alpha; no background, ground plane, cast shadow, floor, extra creature, duplicate, panel, frame, grid, labels, text, watermark, UI, glow, blur, gradient, motion streak, impact flash, particles, weapons or blood.
Sprite constraints: one clear static pose only, all body pieces remain attached to the puppet; preserve the original body proportions, long-arm asymmetry, wood grain, copper thread and small moss marks; do not add or remove body parts.
Pose request — dead-2, almost fallen: fold the puppet down onto its bent knees and one supporting hand, with the torso nearly horizontal and the narrow head close to the ground. The long forward/right arm reaches down toward the right to catch the body; the other arm hangs limp, and the snapped strings trail loosely. Keep the puppet at the same location. This is a further distinct stage after dead-1; body remains complete, attached and opaque, with no breakage or fading.
